metadata.title: Pass 3 reference constants: Fahraeus-Lindqvist apparent blood viscosity fit and hemispherical retinal-cup / arteriovenous geometry for 1959-murray-vascular-cube-law-branching.py

sources.citation: Pries AR, Neuhaus D, Gaehtgens P (1992). Blood viscosity in tube flow: dependence on diameter and hematocrit. American Journal of Physiology - Heart and Circulatory Physiology 263(6):H1770-H1778.
sources.doi_verification: not verified offline during Pass 3 (no network access permitted); recalled from the standard citation

sources.citation: Fahraeus R, Lindqvist T (1931). The viscosity of the blood in narrow capillary tubes. American Journal of Physiology 96(3):562-568.

Hubbard LD, Brothers RJ, King WN, Clegg LX, Klein R, Cooper LS, Sharrett AR, Davis MD, Cai J (1999). Methods for evaluation of retinal microvascular abnormalities associated with hypertension/sclerosis in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study. Ophthalmology 106(12):2269-2280.
sources.used_for: clinical retinal arteriole-to-venule caliber ratio AVR ~ 2/3 (central retinal artery/vein equivalents)

fahraeus_lindqvist_pries_1992_in_vitro_f.variables: D = tube (lumen) diameter in micrometres; eta_rel = apparent viscosity / plasma viscosity at discharge hematocrit H_D = 0.45
fahraeus_lindqvist_pries_1992_in_vitro_f.script_normalisation: eta(r) = eta_murray * eta_rel(2r) / 3.2 with eta_murray = 0.035 P so that the large-vessel limit reproduces Murray (1926a) exactly; only the shape of the curve enters the exponent analysis
fahraeus_lindqvist_pries_1992_in_vitro_f.table_note: values are evaluated from the fit above (parity table for the script's self-test), not independently digitised measurements

generalised_murray_stationarity.power_functional: P(r) = 8 L Q^2 eta(r) / (pi r^4) + b pi r^2 L
generalised_murray_stationarity.log_sensitivity: epsilon(r) = d ln eta / d ln r
generalised_murray_stationarity.optimal_flow: Q*(r) = (pi/2) r^3 sqrt( b / ( eta(r) (4 - epsilon(r)) ) )
generalised_murray_stationarity.local_exponent: gamma_eff(r) = d ln Q* / d ln r  (= 3 for epsilon = 0)

hemispherical_retinal_cup_geometry.eye_radius_note: schematic emmetropic human globe, axial length ~24 mm
hemispherical_retinal_cup_geometry.polar_limit_note: ora serrata lies ~100-110 deg from the posterior pole; growth is clipped at 95 deg
hemispherical_retinal_cup_geometry.geodesic_step: p' = p cos(s/R) + R t sin(s/R);  t' = -(p/R) sin(s/R) + t cos(s/R)
hemispherical_retinal_cup_geometry.tangent_plane_rotation: t_rot = t cos(theta) + (n x t) sin(theta),  n = p/R
hemispherical_retinal_cup_geometry.coupling_rule: veins grow after arteries; at each venous bifurcation the side-branch handedness whose geodesic end-point is farther from the nearest arterial node is kept (repulsive A/V territory exclusion); Murray radii and angles unchanged
